changes: DM sends capture account, session generation, destination recipient/encryption mode and encrypted local-device context. Guards run after file preparation/encryption, through API dispatch/refresh, before cache effects and before detached-window navigation. Unknown conversations are not guessed to be plaintext.

Encrypted DMs now fail closed when crypto/device initialization or recipient keys are unavailable. Removed the RECIPIENT_NO_KEYS plaintext fallback and the not-ready encrypted-conversation fallthrough. Explicitly non-encrypted conversations retain their plaintext send path.

sendWithRetryAndToast supports an optional caller guard before dispatch and after completion, suppressing stale toasts without changing the no-automatic-POST-replay policy. DM send APIs propagate this guard for JSON and multipart requests. Persisted sent plaintext receives the existing cache context guard.

Failed encrypted sends remove their exact queued payload rather than another concurrent send's last entry. Queue access clears entries on session-generation changes as well as device changes. Removed the misleading blanket no-race comment; FIFO echo matching remains a separate limitation.
verification: Store regressions cover missing recipient keys, not-ready crypto/missing device without plaintext dispatch, account/generation/device replacement during encryption, session replacement during file preparation, and late successful/failed encrypted HTTP responses without new-session caching/toasts.

Crypto tests verify exact failed-entry removal among overlapping payloads and old-session cleanup with an unchanged device ID. Shared helper tests cover abandoned dispatch and stale failure-to-toast suppression. The existing detached plaintext send test now supplies explicit plaintext conversation metadata rather than relying on an unknown-conversation fallback.

Initial focused suites passed: 3 files / 66 tests before the final queue/helper regressions were added. A final TypeScript check caught an untyped deferred test promise; fixed its APIResponse generic. Final tsc -b and targeted ESLint passed. Full client suite passed: 229 files / 2229 tests in 46.34s. Vite production web build passed in 702ms. Existing warning categories remain visible.
remaining: This does not retract a write already accepted by the server. Internal Signal/IndexedDB operations, DM edit/create/message-fetch lifecycle races and actual device/logout acceptance still need broader verification.

The sent-plaintext queue still matches WS echoes by FIFO; reversed concurrent commit/echo ordering needs source/version-bound matching. Exact failure cleanup does not prove correct echo attribution. Sender cache at-rest and historical attachment-key behavior remain separate concerns.
Overall P0-P11 remains incomplete. No server migration, commit, push, merge, Windows packaging or production release performed.
